Market stance

The group heads into Tuesday's midterms defensive — Prof calls the Nasdaq's third 10% correction of 2026 at its 200-day line, Venu sees distribution and a likely 200-day test, and iain is sitting out bounces into declining averages — while Enrich splits Tuesday's tape into upside names to hold and downside names to avoid, and the only two-trader agreement is SPOT's base curling up.

Key watches

Catalysts

  • U.S. midterm elections, Tue 11/3 — the week's centerpiece; Enrich adds Iran as the headline risk that survives the vote
  • JOLTS + factory orders, Tue 10 AM ET — the macro line for Tuesday, carried from Enrich's massive-week list
  • PLTR Q3: double beat + raised guide, reported after Monday's close — EPS $0.44 vs $0.41, revenue $2.313B vs $2.183B (Prof's figures); Tuesday's open prices it, since no after-hours price appears in this window
  • AAPL earnings, due Monday after the close — no result appears in any trader's visible post in this window, so none is stated
  • AMD earnings week — Remz's make-or-break frame from Nov 1, now resolved on the downside by Monday's close below $500
  • CAVA earnings week — DiCarlo's double smart-money zone setup, already up 20%+ since he posted it
  • AMAT earnings next week — the clock on Remz's 20-point downside gap-fill short idea

Market — SPY · QQQ · IWM · TLT

Macro overlay — from their posts, not our data
A midterm-eve window with the group defensive after Monday's follow-through selling. Prof supplies the tape read: the Nasdaq is at its 200-day line in its third 10% correction of 2026, with thousands of momentum stocks down 50–70% and sentiment “awful.” Venu supplies the distribution read: the Nasdaq is facing rejection near Friday's highs after a gap down, and there is a good chance it tests the 200-day average — the same line Prof names. iain supplies the process read: bounces into declining averages keep getting smoked, leaders like NTRA are trading like meme coins after wiping out 26 days of gains in one candle, and his plan is to sit out until charts stop looking like they need medical attention — small size, tight risk, and only when the setup is right. Enrich supplies the split tape: his Tuesday watchlist puts BE, TSLA, CVNA, PFE and MMM upside and DELL, AMD, HPE and SNOW downside, with the warning that oversold RSI alone is not a bottom — he wants higher lows, 9EMA reclaims with volume and relative strength before trusting a bounce, and he flags Iran as the headline risk that outlasts the midterms. Remz supplies the short side: AMAT as a 20-point downside gap fill into next week's earnings, and a $20,000 day built on DELL, AMD and $P. DiCarlo supplies the counterweight: INTC's long-term buy zone at $50, CAVA's double smart-money zone into earnings week, TEM breaking out toward a short-term target after a 30%+ run, and MSTR's $400+ 24-month target. Your process gives no clean qualifier today either: SPOT's base curl is the closest, but the 52-week high 655.32 sits 10.30% above; TEM's breakout is real but extended after a 30%+ run; and the rest of the tape is tests to survive — SPY on its 30-week line, AMD below $500, INTC between $70 and $50, PLTR's beat awaiting Tuesday's open. The discipline is in the framing: hold-or-fail levels (SPY 751.30, AMD 440, INTC 70/50, PLTR 184.99) decide the week, while RKLB, BE, DELL and AMAT are called out as broken or downside, not entries.

Sean — no new post in this window: his newest visible post is still the Oct 29 system post, and the Oct 28–29 posts are unchanged from yesterday's read — no ticker, no level, so Sean has no row today, and readability is not the constraint, content is.

iain — process posts, no new ticker: Nov 2, 21:30 UTC — why he watches the slope of moving averages, not just price vs the average: after a sharp selloff, stocks rally back toward declining MAs, “but those areas can still act as overhead resistance” (quoted to the visible cutoff). Venu — correction discipline, no new ticker: Nov 2, 16:12 UTC — the most expensive habit is feeling the need to participate in every move: a 10–15% rally without you tempts you to chase stocks in downtrends and ignore risk (quoted to the visible cutoff).

SPY carries iain's and Enrich's market-wide caution; QQQ carries Prof's and Venu's Nasdaq-specific reads.

DiCarlo's SPY/QQQ monthly-red read from Nov 1 is superseded by Prof's and Venu's fresh Nasdaq reads and is not repeated. Enrich's 11/2 watchlist (TSLA, RKLB, NBIS, SKHY, MU, BE, SPOT) is superseded by his 11/3 watchlist — only names re-listed today get panels from it.
  • Badge key: Setup describes structure only (green = constructive, amber = pending confirmation, red = broken/extended/avoid). Coverage counts the traders behind a name and is always gray — “Chart only” means no trader mentioned it and implies nothing about the setup. The stage pill next to each ticker (30-week MA basis) is the only place a stage label appears; it is kept out of the prose and the setup badges, and traders' own quoted words are exempt.
  • Level strength: Strong = 2+ confluent anchors (52w high/low, 3m swing, 50-day EMA, 30-week MA, 50-week EMA, trader-stated) within 0.75%, or a 52w extreme with 3+ weekly touches in the past year. Moderate = 1 anchor or 2–3 touches. Light = anything else. Touches count weeks whose high or low came within 0.75% of the level. Duplicate prices merge into one row carrying both labels. AMAT shows no invalidation row: it is a short idea, and there is no long thesis below to invalidate.
  • Trader charts: none embedded this edition. No trader posted a retrievable chart image for a covered name in the visible posts this window, so no trader chart is embedded rather than risking a wrong one.
  • Chart verification gate: every plotted line's endpoint was checked against levels.json before the HTML was built — all 87 computable lines passed within 0.5%. The 30-week MA is a true trailing mean over full 30-week windows only.
